title: Cross-Lingual Feature Alignment in SAEs: Do the Same Semantic Features Appear in Both English and French Text?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if features are language-specific, safety interventions based on feature steering in one language will not generalize to other languages, directly undermining multilingual safety guarantees. Each link is explicit and independently defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training or loading SAEs on a multilingual model (mGPT), running automated feature labeling, constructing matched English/French concept pairs, and computing Jaccard similarity of active latents. The multilingual SAE pipeline is not as well-documented as English-only and involves multiple specialized tools. Advanced for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple workstreams: SAE training/loading, feature labeling, cross-lingual dataset construction, similarity computation. The deliverable exists but requires resolving several dependencies (correct multilingual model, matched concept pairs, labeling pipeline). Sustained effort beyond a single clean experiment.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple recent papers directly address cross-lingual SAE feature alignment: 'Sparse Autoencoders Can Capture Language-Specific Concepts Across Diverse Languages' (arXiv:2507.11230) uses SAE-LAPE to identify language-specific features; 'Uncovering Cross-Linguistic Disparities in LLMs using Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2507.18918) systematically analyzes cross-lingual SAE representations; 'Disentangling concept semantics via multilingual averaging in Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2508.14275) isolates concept semantics across languages. The core question of whether SAE features align across languages has been extensively studied with more languages and models than the proposed English/French comparison.
